capture.text: No guardrail on the north side of level five by the stair opening. Nobody is working up there right now but that needs to be fixed today before the deck crew comes back.

capture.text: Housekeeping is bad in the north stair, boxes and banding all over the landing. Get Jim from ACME Cleaning to deal with it.

capture.text: We spent most of the afternoon on the extra dewatering at the north footing that the super asked for. I will get you the crew hours tomorrow once I check the timecards.

note: Hours are the whole point of the ticket and this note does not give them. Inventing a number here would fabricate a claim, so the draft must stay incomplete.

capture.text: Crew of four on the level three hangers all day, about thirty two hours. Normal production, on schedule.

note: Hours alone do not make a T&M ticket. This is base scope work reported at the end of the day, which is a daily log. Reading every mention of hours as a claim would flood the GC with tickets nobody owes.

capture.text: Per Sam's direction Tuesday we reworked the hanger layout above corridor two after the duct moved. Eight hours, two men. We think this is extra, Sam thinks part of it is ours. Filing it either way so the clock does not run out.

note: A contested ticket is still a ticket. The disagreement belongs in the signer's dispute, not in the interpreter deciding not to file it.

capture.text: We hit rock at the north footing, a good two feet below what C-201 shows. Excavator is stopped. This is going to be extra and it is going to move the foundation pour.

note: A condition nobody drew, stopping work, with cost and time consequences. Incomplete because nothing in the note prices it, and a change priced at a silent zero is worse than one not priced at all.

capture.text: Owner walked the lobby this morning and asked us to swap the terrazzo for polished concrete. Nadia said to price it and she will issue the directive.

note: Directed by the owner, named, and explicitly to be priced. The cause field is the whole argument in a dispute, so getting it wrong is expensive.

capture.text: The duct above corridor two does not clear the structure the way it is drawn. Need the architect to tell us which one moves.

note: A coordination conflict with no direction given and no scope agreed is a question, not a change. Reading every clash as a change event would have a contractor pricing work nobody asked for.

capture.text: Add the extra bollards at the loading dock. Four of them, same as the ones at the north entry. Somebody decided they were needed.

capture.text: Rae, can you get me the updated mechanical coordination drawings before Friday's OAC. Nothing urgent, just need them in hand.

note: A named person owing a named thing by a date. Not an RFI, because nothing is being asked of the design team, and forcing it into one distorts the RFI log.

capture.text: OAC this morning, Priya, Ali and Sam present. Went through the steel sequence, the curtain wall mock-up date, and the level 2 ceiling heights. Curtain wall carries to next week.

note: A meeting held with attendance and business, one item explicitly carried forward. Incomplete because the note gives no scheduled date field and inventing one would misdate the minutes.

capture.text: Send Vega Steel a formal notice that they have been off site four working days and the erection sequence is now behind. Certified mail, copy the owner.

note: Formal, contractual, with a delivery method named. The delivery method matters: a notice nobody can prove was served is not a notice.

capture.text: Tell Tomas the crane is booked Thursday morning so he should plan around it.

note: Passing on scheduling information is a task, not correspondence. Correspondence is a contractual act somebody points at later, and treating every message as one buries the letters that matter.

capture.text: We had a laceration on level three about twenty minutes ago. One of Vega's guys caught his forearm on a sheared stud. First aid on site, he is fine, back to work. I called Tomas and the safety manager already.

note: Incomplete on purpose. An incident is a legal document from the moment it is written, so a draft that looks finished invites somebody to sign it without reading, and OSHA recordability is never a guess an agent should make.

capture.text: A bundle of rebar shifted off the forks on the east lay-down and came down about six feet from two of our guys. Nobody was hit. We shut the area and re-banded the load.

note: Nobody hurt and nobody hit. Reading this as an observation would lose the one record type that has to exist for it, and near misses are the cheapest safety data on a job.

capture.text: The guardrail at the level five stair opening is missing again. Nobody near it right now but it needs to go back up today.

note: An unsafe condition with nothing having happened is a safety observation. Filing it as an incident inflates the incident rate a contractor is judged on, and that number decides whether they can bid work.

note: A named inspection with a result and specific deficiencies. This one is complete because the note carries everything the record needs to hand somebody the ball.
